title: Long-Term Vessel Trajectory Imputation with Physics-Guided Diffusion Probabilistic Model

problem.claim: Missing AIS data creates long-term gaps in vessel trajectories, with potential collision and illicit-activity security concerns.

gap.claim: Existing imputation approaches are constrained by vehicle-based low-sampling trajectories and do not adequately address maritime transportation characteristics or long-term missing scenarios.

contributions.claim: A generative framework is proposed for long-term vessel trajectory imputation.

The framework uses a pre-trained trajectory embedding block and a diffusion-based conditional generation model incorporating transformer-encoded observed trajectories, historical vessel trajectories, and external factors.
A physics-guided discriminator imposes kinematic constraints between locations and angles during training to improve continuity of imputed trajectories.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe their long-term vessel trajectory imputation framework as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that comprehensive experiments and analysis on a real-world AIS dataset confirm the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

narrative_sequence.summary: AIS-based vessel position information supports maritime traffic management.
Missing AIS data causes long-term trajectory gaps and related security concerns.
Existing approaches are limited by vehicle-oriented low-sampling trajectories and long-term maritime imputation requirements.
The proposed framework models irregular vessel tracks with trajectory embeddings, conditional diffusion generation, and physics-guided kinematic constraints.
Experiments and analysis on a real-world AIS dataset are reported as confirming effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: The framework accounts for irregular vessel tracks and uses kinematic constraints to improve continuity.

interpretation.claim: Domain-specific structural and physical constraints can be integrated into generative trajectory imputation.

application.claim: For irregular movement data, combine learned generative modeling with domain constraints that reflect continuity or feasible motion.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond vessel trajectories or the reported AIS setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset size, missingness configurations, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide implementation, training, or reproducibility details.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported effectiveness.
